dedupe_keys.name: egress cell devs models emergency crowd evacuation suite jafer and lawler

description: A suite of 12 emergency egress models built on the Cellular Discrete-Event System Specification (Cell-DEVS) formalism and an open-source DEVS simulation environment, published by Shafagh Jafer and Ryan Lawler of Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in the journal SIMULATION in 2016. The models represent random and controlled human movement, psychological conditions such as herd following and panic, and the actions of authorities guiding a crowd. The authors compare evacuation speed under the different egress methods so the suite can support training of first responders and decision support, as an economical alternative to physical exercises. The article states that the outcome is on a public repository, which holds the model files for the DEVS community and public safety authorities. Coverage: generic crowded rooms and open areas on a grid, not a specific site. Format and access: free GitHub repository and an article whose full text is behind the publisher. Caveats: the repository README is empty and no licence is stated, so inputs, dependencies and any validation against real evacuations were not checked. Useful for testing crowd evacuation strategies in buildings and public space in a discrete-event simulation; related records are not yet linked.
